# wallix.bastion.profile

Manage user profiles on a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.1.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Create, update or delete a user profile on a WALLIX Bastion.
- A profile gives its users rights on the Bastion web interface and API, and can restrict the IP addresses they connect from and the user and target groups they see.
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_profile` Terraform resource.
- The built-in profiles (`user`, `product_administrator`, ...) cannot be changed.

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Options left unset keep their current value on the Bastion.
- The profile is looked up by [`profile_name`](#parameter-profile-name), so it cannot be renamed with this module.
- The Bastion refuses [`gui_transmission`](#parameter-gui-transmission) rights that exceed [`gui_features`](#parameter-gui-features), and rights that exceed those of the API user.
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: Profile of operators who manage devices and see audit data
  wallix.bastion.profile:
    profile_name: operators
    description: Device operators
    gui_features:
      wab_audit: view
      devices: modify
      target_groups: view
    gui_transmission:
      devices: view
    dashboards: [audit]
    ip_limitation: 10.0.0.0/8
    target_access: true
    target_groups_limitation:
      enabled: true
      target_groups: [linux-servers, windows-servers]
      default_target_group: linux-servers

- name: Remove the target group limitation
  wallix.bastion.profile:
    profile_name: operators
    target_groups_limitation:
      enabled: false

- name: Remove a profile
  wallix.bastion.profile:
    profile_name: operators
    state: absent
```

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated.<br><br>Returned: when the profile already existed and [`state=present`](#parameter-state)<br><br>Sample: `["gui_features", "dashboards"]` |
| <a id="return-profile"></a>**profile** | `dict` | The profile as returned by the Bastion API after the change. Rights not granted are `null`.<br>In check mode, the expected profile. `null` when [`state=absent`](#parameter-state).<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-profile) |

```yaml
  credential_recovery: null

  profiles: null
  system_audit: null

  target_groups: view
  user_groups: null

gui_transmission:

  authorizations: null
  backup: null
  credential_recovery: null
  devices: view
  profiles: null
  system_audit: null
  system_settings: null
  target_groups: null
  user_groups: null
  users: null
  wab_settings: null
id: 1a0f76a4310471af005056b66c8b
ip_limitation: 10.0.0.0/8
profile_name: operators
target_access: true

  default_target_group: linux-servers
  enabled: true
  target_groups:
  - linux-servers
  - windows-servers
url: https://bastion.example.com/api/v3.12/profiles/1a0f76a4310471af005056b66c8b
user_groups_limitation:
  enabled: false
```
